goal: The dash node is laid out with the real parts, proved in cardboard in the car, and its carrier panels are cut, deburred and painted.
where: bench, then the driver footwell and under the dash for the mock-up
tools:
Cardboard, marker, craft knife, tape
Steel rule and square
Drill and bits, step bit
Jigsaw or hacksaw, files, deburring tool
Centre punch
Phone camera
before:
E12 - the car starts and charges on the new backbone
C2 - the panel stock (P090) and paint (P093) are bought
C1's measurements in hand: the M-1 dash envelope and the wideband gauge's hiding place
The interior is still out (S1), so the footwell and dash rail are open
Master disconnect open while you reach around the temporary distribution post: the 2 AWG feed is live there (E10, E4)
know:
The dash node is everything that hangs off the PMU in one place: the PMU-24, the always-hot busbar, the ground bus, fuse blocks A and B, the inline fuse holders, nine relay sockets, the wake strip, a perfboard and the wideband gauge [work E13]
Nine relay sockets at the node, not seven: K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13 and the two seat relays K14 K15 added by D-469 [relays K14, K15]
Sixteen receptacles sit at the dash post: L1-P DTP04-4P, L1-S1 DT04-12P, L1-S2 DT04-12P, L2-P DTP04-4P, L2-M DT04-8P, L2-S DT04-6P, L3-P DTP04-2P, L3-M DT04-2P, L3-S1 DT04-12P, L3-S2 DT04-12P, L3-S3 DT04-8P, L4-P DTP04-4P, L4-M DT04-12P, L4-S DT04-8P, L4-S2 DT04-8P, L2-R DT04-4P [housings]
Leave panel room beside L1-S1 / L1-S2 for four more DT04-12P receptacles for the engine swap - five if engine block 02.16 was answered (a) [work E13, engine D-443]
Water runs down from the cowl seam and the windscreen corners: every wire enters the PMU and the node from below or with a drip loop, nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell, and the PMU 39-way faces down or sideways, never up [rules water-ingress]
What CK04 found (where the water goes with the dash out) moves a bracket now for free [checks CK04]
The PMU stands on three M6 x 12 mm stand-offs for airflow [parts P060]
The busbar is the Blue Sea 2300, 10-gang 150 A with cover: one always-hot bar and one ground bus, both covered [parts P007]
The DCU tail must reach the centre stack: the node has to sit close enough along RT11, which is measured at M-2 [routes RT11, housings DP-DCU-B]
Receptacle clips: 1027-003-1200 fits the 2, 4, 6 and 12-way and every DTP; the 8-way receptacles take the 8-way clip - four of them are at the post (L2-M, L3-S3, L4-S, L4-S2), D1 and D2 are at the sill; both use an 11 mm hole - confirm on the clip in hand [parts P030, P162]
Nothing here is measured by anyone but you: the cardboard in the car is the proof, not the drawing [R11]
done_when: Every part has a place on painted panels that passed the cardboard mock-up in the car: the PMU lever swings its full arc, there is 60 mm clear behind every receptacle, both fuse blocks can be reached, and nothing sits in the lowest 50 mm.
if_not: If it does not all fit inside the M-1 space, do not thin the clearances: split it across more panels or move a panel, mock it again, and raise a note in the app with a photo. If RT11 is long for the DCU tail, raise a note before cutting metal.
record: Tick the row. Add a note with the photos of the cardboard mock-up in the car and the finished panels.

goal: Every part of the dash node is mounted on its panel and every relay socket and fuse position carries its label.
tools:
Screwdrivers and small sockets
Torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N·m (P046)
Wire strippers and flush cutters (P043)
Label printer with the node labels from E6 (P041)
Paint pen (P082)
before:
E13 - the panels are cut and painted
E6 - the node labels are printed
Nothing is connected to the car: this is bench work
know:
The PMU stands on three M6 stand-offs [work E14, parts P060]
Five 40 A-class MAXI holders (P189): F30 feeds block A, F31 feeds K11 terminal 30, F32 sits at K11 terminal 87 and feeds block B - 40 A fuses (P190); F35 and F36 feed the seat relays K14 / K15 - 25 A fuses (P191) [fuses F30, F31, F32, F35, F36, D-467, D-469]
The fuse sits at the bar so the only wire protected by the Class-T alone is a short stub: each busbar-fed inline holder (F12, F22, F23) has its 14 AWG lead cut to about 50 mm, never more than 180 mm [node_conductors N75, N87]
Block A is on the busbar: position 1 F2, 2 F3, 3 F19, 4 F13 (no fuse). Block B is behind K11: position 1 F1, 2 F5 (no fuse) [fuses]
The 8-position strip is full: seven wake inputs and the common rail [parts P068]
Labels come from the label columns: K1 POPUP-L · K2 POPUP-R · K3 HATCH-REL · K4 FUEL-REL · K11 HEAD-UNIT · K12 WASHER · K13 FUEL-PUMP · K14 SEAT-D · K15 SEAT-P [relays]
Fuse labels at the node: F1 HEAD-UNIT · F2 DIAG · F3 SWITCH · F12 INTERIOR · F13 — · F15 ALT-EXCITE · F16 DISPLAY · F19 COURTESY · F20 WIDEBAND · F21 KICK-DOWN · F22 DCU-CONST · F23 WAKE · F5 SENSOR-2 · F30 BLOCK-A-FEED · F31 K11-FEED · F32 BLOCK-B-FEED · F33 RELEASE · F35 SEAT-D · F36 SEAT-P · F37 POPUP-CMD [fuses]

done_when: Every part is fixed and does not move when pushed, every relay socket and every fuse position has its printed label beside it (the empty ones too), and no fuse or relay is fitted yet.
if_not: A part that fouls another: stop, go back to the cardboard (E13) rather than bending a bracket. A missing label: print it from the relays / fuses label column, never hand-write it.
record: Tick the row.

goal: The wake strip carries its seven diodes and bleed resistor, the two wake sense stages are built on the perfboard to the wake_stages table, the two bias resistors are fitted, and the bench check CK12 is read.
tools:
Soldering iron and solder (P044)
Flush cutters, needle-nose pliers (P043)
Multimeter: ohms, diode test, DC volts (P045)
Heat gun (P042)
A 12 V bench supply or the battery through a fused lead for CK12
before:
E14 - the strip and perfboard are mounted
A10 - the stage values are in the record (they are: the wake_stages table)
Eye protection while soldering and clipping leads
know:
The PMU wakes when pin 7 (+12V SW) goes high. Seven sources are OR-ed onto it through one diode each, so no source can feed another [pins 7]
Strip inputs: 1 ACC (L3-S1 12) · 2 RUN (L3-S2 1) · 3 door stage · 4 horn / hazard / wink stage · 5 O22 keep-alive (pin 8) · 6 brake plunger (L3-S1 7) · 7 DCU wake request (DP-DCU 6) [node_conductors N33-N37, N63, N76]
Seven 1N5819, band (cathode) toward the common rail; the rail goes to pin 7; 10 kΩ from the rail to the GND bus [node_conductors N38, work E15]
The two sense stages are a comparator design now: one LM2903 DIP-8 serves both, U1A the door line (A6, pin 18), U1B the horn / hazard / wink line (A8, pin 19). The work row still says NPN sense stages: the table is newer and wins [wake_stages WS15, WS25]
Both stages are fed from F23, 3 A, constant from the busbar [fuses F23, node_conductors N87]
The base clamps are 1N4148, never a Schottky: a 1N5819 leaks hot and loses the pulse at 85 °C [wake_stages WS19]
The edge capacitors are 2.2 µF film (P158); the value is still to be confirmed against the PMU boot time CK12 reads [wake_stages WS17]
The threshold divider resistors WS14 / WS24 are 1 % parts [wake_stages WS14]
Bias: 100 kΩ from pin 15 (+5 V) to pin 35 (A15) and 100 kΩ from pin 15 to pin 22 (A16), so a broken wire reads 0, not OFF [node_conductors N39]
At rest the door and A8 lines sit at 0.166 x the F23 voltage (about 1.99 V at 12.0 V); the comparator threshold is 0.115 x [wake_stages WS12, WS13]
The pin-out of the LM2903 and the 2N3904 is not in the record: read each off its datasheet before soldering [gap]
done_when: Seven diodes read forward toward the rail and blocked the other way; every resistor measured before fitting; CK12 read on the bench: at rest no wake, any door or A8 switch wakes, the three unknowns (i)-(iii) written down.
if_not: A stage that does not wake: check the comparator supply (F23) and the divider node (0.115 x F23), then the 2.2 µF and the follower. If the unpowered PMU pin reads under 200 kΩ to ground at CK12 (i), stop: WS12 may have to drop - raise a note with the reading. Do not put the node in the car on a failing CK12.
record: Tick the row. Enter the CK12 readings as a note: (i) ohms pin 18 and pin 19 to ground with the PMU unpowered, (ii) the lowest pin 7 voltage that switches the PMU on and its current at 12 V, (iii) seconds from pin 7 high to O22 on.

goal: All 39 cavities of the PMU connector are terminated, locked and pull-tested, each on 18 in of labelled wire.
tools:
Open-barrel ratchet crimper, 1.5 mm and 2.8 mm dies (P039)
Wire strippers and flush cutters (P043)
Paint pen (P082)
Label printer (P041)
Heat gun for the label shrink (P042)
Good light and a magnifier
before:
E15 - the wake parts are built
CK24 read at M-1: the terminal part numbers on the spare PMU housings (1.5 mm and 2.8 mm) and which terminal pin 15 takes
Practice crimps pulled on scrap with this crimper and these terminals
The connector is off the PMU and nothing is powered
Eye protection
know:
The PMU-24 has one 39-way connector plus the +12 V stud. Every one of the 39 positions is used [rules spare-capacity]
Three cavity sizes: 11 large (pins 1, 2, 12, 13, 14, 25, 26, 27, 28, 38, 39 - the 2.8 mm die), 27 small (the 1.5 mm die) and one medium, pin 15, whose terminal and die the record does not name - confirm from CK24 [parts P039, checks CK24]
Cavity numbers are the numbers moulded into the connector itself: read them off the part, never mirror a drawing [rules cavity-numbers]
Colours by family: RED power outputs, ORN the 15 A outputs on 14 AWG, GRY analog inputs, BLU wake, PNK the +5 V reference, YEL / GRN CAN high / low, BLK ground [colours]
Large pins carry up to 25 A, the 14 AWG ORN pins 15 A, the 16 AWG RED output pins 7 A [pins hw_max_a]
The +12 V stud is not in this connector: it takes the 2 AWG from the busbar at E17 / E24 [pins STUD]
Pin 25, the ground, lands on the GND bus within 6 in: it is the one wire that will be cut shorter than 18 in when it lands [pins 25]
The two CAN pairs are hand-twisted: 23 with 36 (CAN1), 24 with 37 (CAN2) [colours, pins 23, 24]
It is terminated once and never reopened [work E16]
The SICMA terminals have no parts row and no strip length in the record: use the terminals that came with the PMU connector and the strip length your practice crimps proved [gap]
done_when: 39 wires, each labelled, each clicked in and pulled; the secondary lock is on; no wire moves under a firm pull; the lever latched once fully on the PMU with a clear arc.
if_not: A terminal that does not click or pulls out: do not force it and do not re-use it - cut it off, crimp a new one. A wire in the wrong cavity: stop, do not pick at it with a pin - raise a note; the record names no removal tool for this connector.
record: Tick the row.

goal: Every node conductor is run, spliced and landed, every receptacle at the post is pinned, plugged and wedge-locked, and the ICU and DCU tails are made.
tools:
Deutsch solid-contact 4-indent crimper, sizes 12 / 16 (P038)
Ratchet crimper for heat-shrink terminals and butt splices (P171)
Open-barrel crimper for the relay socket terminals (P039)
Wire strippers, flush cutters (P043)
Heat gun (P042)
Soldering iron (P044)
Contact removal tools, size 16 (P031, P032)
Label printer (P041)
Multimeter on continuity (P045)
Torque wrench (P046)
before:
E16 - the 39-way is terminated
E15 - the wake strip and stages are built
CK08 (M-3, the pop-up motors) is read before the pop-up conductors N08-N15 and N105 are landed
Nothing is powered; the 39-way is off the PMU
Eye protection for crimping
know:
A receptacle is the box-side half (DT04 / DTP04, pin contacts); the leg plugs (DT06, socket contacts) are made at E20-E23 [housings]
Every splice at the node is a sealed crimp butt splice with adhesive heat-shrink [work E17, parts P078]
An unfused tap off an output is 14 AWG up to its fuse (the holder's own lead), 16 AWG after it [node_conductors N19, N85]
CAN2 never leaves the dash: one twisted pair from pins 24 / 37 to a splice, pairs on to DP-ICU-A 4 / 5, DP-DCU 4 / 5 and the wideband gauge, and a 120 Ω resistor at the end of the run [node_conductors N55, N74, D-346]
The A4 and A5 inputs carry the inhibitor switch alone since D-487: pin 17 goes to L1-S1 11 only and pin 31 to L1-S2 7 only. Rows N40 / N41 still name L2-S 1 / 2, which are the pop-up up commands now [cavities L2-S 1, L2-S 2, pins 17, 31]
The DCU plugs in later (E26): its two tails end in DT06 plugs at the centre stack and are dust-capped until then [housings DP-DCU, DP-DCU-B, D-472]
The ICU tails are 150 mm from the post [housings DP-ICU-A, D-270]
The DCU tail length is the post to centre-stack run RT11 and the DP-DIAG tail is the run to the glovebox RT12: neither is measured - confirm [routes RT11, RT12]
DT size-16 contacts seal on 14-20 AWG and carry 13 A; DTP size-12 contacts seal on 10-14 AWG and carry 25 A [series DT, DTP]
The seat-feed tails (N108, N109, N112) and the comfort grounds (N102) are routed at E38: at this row their relays are wired and the tails left labelled [work E38]
The load-dump TVS (P136) goes across the PMU main feed at the module; no row says which way round or on which studs - read its datasheet [parts P136, gap]
done_when: Every row of node_conductors is in place and labelled at both ends, every receptacle cavity holds a pin or a sealing plug, every wedgelock is in, the two ICU tails and the two DCU tails end in plugs.
if_not: A contact in the wrong cavity: release it with the removal tool (P031 / P032), never pull the wire. A conductor with no home in the lists: stop and raise a note - do not improvise a splice.
record: Tick the row.

goal: The finished node is proved: every PMU cavity reaches what the tables say and nothing else, nothing leaks to ground, the relays and fuses are fitted, every wire is labelled and the panels are photographed.
tools:
Multimeter with a continuity beeper and a megohm range (P045)
Two sharp probe leads and a back-probe pin that fits a DT pin without spreading a socket
The pin list on the laptop or phone
Phone camera
before:
E17 - every conductor is landed
The 39-way is off the PMU; no leg, relay or fuse is fitted; the node is not powered
know:
Continuity is taken with the meter on its beeper [work E18]
Isolation means open: more than 1 MΩ. Any lower reading is a stray strand [work E18]
Nine relays at the node, all the same part (P003): K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13 K14 K15. The work row lists five and calls K3 / K4 the luxury package's; the relays table has all nine fitted this build [relays, parts P003, D-451, D-469]
Blade fuses come from the drawer, one of every rating in the fuses table [parts P141]
Two blade positions stay empty and keep their labels: F13 (block A position 4) and F5 (block B position 2) [fuses F13, F5]
Through a diode the beeper is one-way: the wake strip inputs and the O2 / O3 pop-up coil taps read as a diode, not as a short [node_conductors N09, N38]
Pin 15 reaches pins 35 and 22 through 100 kΩ each and the oil node through 100 Ω: that is correct, not a fault [node_conductors N39]
The CAN2 pair should read about 120 Ω with nothing plugged in: the one resistor at the node [node_conductors N74]
done_when: All 39 cavities pass continuity and the three must-not-reach touches each; every power cavity reads open to its neighbours and to the ground bus; nine relays and every LIVE fuse are in; photos taken.
if_not: A missing continuity: find it now - a contact not seated or a splice not crimped. Any isolation reading under 1 MΩ: stop and find the strand before any power is applied. Do not go on to E19 with an open item.
record: Tick the row. Add the photos as a note.

goal: The sleeping current of the finished dash node is measured and is 50 mA or less.
tools:
Multimeter with a fused 10 A range and a mA range (P045)
A 12 V supply for the node through a fused lead
before:
E18 - the node passed continuity and isolation, relays and fuses fitted
CK12 read (E15)
No leg plugged in; the DCU tails capped
know:
Target 30 mA or less; accept 50 mA or less [work E19, loads LD17, D-280]
What should be drawing: the PMU asleep (no manual figure; a bench report says under 20 mA) and the wake stages (under 0.2 mA). K11 is open when asleep. The DCU is not plugged in yet [loads LD17]
The PMU sleeps when nothing on the wake strip is high; with no key, door or A8 input the keep-alive drops 30 s after the last change [rules sleep]
On a 40 Ah pack 150 mA is about 11 days and 20 mA about 80 days [checks CK02]
This is the PMU's share; the whole-car figure is read later at E29 [checks CK02]
It cannot be re-taken once the dash is closed without undoing the install [work E19]
The record does not name the bench supply for this test, nor what configuration the PMU carries before E25: with pin 7 low it should be asleep - confirm [gap]
done_when: A steady reading of 50 mA or less with the PMU asleep, entered in the app.
if_not: Above 50 mA: lift the wake-strip branches one at a time (inputs 1 to 7, then F23, F22, F12) and watch the reading to find the branch. Do not close the dash on a failing number: raise a note with the readings.
record: Enter the reading in mA (this row takes a value).

goal: Harness leg L3, the dash leg, is cut, labelled, pinned into its five plugs, ended at its switches and branch receptacles, and tested end to end.
where: bench - a board or floor long enough for the full-scale layout
tools:
Deutsch solid-contact 4-indent crimper, sizes 12 / 16 (P038)
Wire strippers 10-22 AWG, flush cutters (P043)
Ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices, rings and spades (P171)
Heat gun (P042)
Soldering iron and solder (P044)
Multimeter: continuity beeper, ohms (P045)
Label printer with flexible-ID tape (P041)
Contact removal tools, size 16 (P031, P032) and size 12 (P033)
Tape measure, and a board or floor long enough to lay the leg full-scale
Paint pen (P082)
before:
E19 - the dash node passed its sleeping-current test
G13 - the cut lengths are derived from the measured routes (C1, M-2)
E7 - the ladder resistor sub-assemblies are built and bagged
CK10 read: the ignition switch IG contact holds through START - take it before this leg is crimped
CK17 and CK18 read: the light switch and stalk contact tables - the ladders are built to what they found
E5 - Deutsch practice done
Eye protection for crimping and clipping
know:
Cut length is 1.5 x the measured route; the margin is that factor, no extra loop is added [rules cut-list, D-202]
Every wire is labelled at both ends the moment it is cut, printed tape, the same pair read in opposite order: O8 / L2-M-1 at one end, L2-M-1 / O8 at the other; a capped far end reads <cavity> / CAPPED [rules label-format]
The leg side is the PLUG (DT06 / DTP06) and takes SOCKET contacts; a branch-end receptacle (DT04 / DTP04) takes PIN contacts [housings, work E20]
A CAPPED wire is cut, labelled and terminated exactly like a LIVE one [work E20]
Cavity numbers are the ones moulded into the housing: read them off the part [rules cavity-numbers]
DT size-16 contacts take 14-20 AWG and carry 13 A; DTP size-12 contacts take 10-14 AWG and carry 25 A [series DT, DTP]
Where a device keeps its factory plug, the plug is cut from the old harness with 150 mm of factory lead and each lead is joined to its new wire with a sealed butt splice; a stud or blade gets a heat-shrink ring or spade [rules device-end]
The factory plugs stay on the old harness until their circuit migrates (E27 / E28): the record does not say at which row each factory-lead splice is made, so at the bench those ends are left cut to length, labelled and insulated [work E27, E28, gap]
L3 has five plugs at the post - L3-P, L3-M, L3-S1, L3-S2, L3-S3 - and four branch-end receptacles: L3-BLW at the HVAC case, L3-CMF behind the centre stack, L3-MOD and L3-RDR behind the dash [housings]
L3-S2 3-6 and L3-S3 5-8 are sealing plugs: the window commands and mirror lines run in the DCU tail from the node, not in this leg [cavities L3-S2 3, L3-S3 5, D-472]
The seat receptacles and comfort-return harness (L3-SD, L3-SP, L3-SDM, L3-SPM) are E38 and the speaker runs are E41: not this row [work E38, E41]
F24, 3 A sealed inline, sits in the leg behind the lower dash where the light-switch and brake-wake branch leaves the L3-S2 2 wire [fuses F24, D-412]
The ignition switch is a new electrical portion (1981-83 type, P086); the light switch, both stalks and the horn pad are the car's own, kept [devices DV18, DV19, DV20, DV22, DV23]
The wiper stalk WASH contact carries two wires: the ladder leg to L3-S1 4 and a plain wire to L3-S2 9, the washer relay coil return [devices DV22, work E20]
WASH leg value: the ladders table says 470 Ω + 1N4148; the cavity and device rows still say 1.8 kΩ + 1N5819. Build to the E7 sub-assembly made from the ladders table - confirm before soldering [ladders A2 WASH, cavities L3-S1 4]
Horn 8.2 kΩ and the two wink resistors (18 kΩ left, 33 kΩ right) all join onto the L3-S1 11 wire; the wink resistors are on the plate board, and the plate's 4-way header J2 gives pin 1 → L3-S1 9, pin 2 → L3-S1 10, pin 3 → L3-S1 11, pin 4 → dash ground [devices DV24, D-504]
The hazard switch gets a 47 kΩ baseline to column ground at the switch, beside its 4.7 kΩ [cavities L3-S1 6, D-368]
The brake wake is a spare adjustable plunger switch (P084) on the pedal, fed through F24, not the brake lamp switch [cavities L3-S1 7, D-278]
Ladder check: each state within 2 % of its table value at the leg-side cavity [work E20]
Column and pedal fasteners, clip counts and the factory wire colours at the kept switches are not in this row's tables: the device rows give the terminal by function only [gap]
done_when: Every L3 cavity is continuous to its own far end and to nothing else, isolation is open, each ladder state fitted so far reads within 2 % of its value, every end is labelled, branch receptacles are dust-capped, and the leg is bundled every 150 mm but not wrapped.
if_not: A contact in the wrong cavity: release it with the removal tool, never pull the wire. A ladder state off by more than 2 %: measure the resistor alone, then the joint. A length that comes up short on the layout: stop, re-measure the route, raise a note.
record: Tick the row.

goal: Harness leg L2, the front leg, is cut, labelled, pinned into its four plugs, spliced at the nose and ended at every front device, and tested.

Deutsch solid-contact 4-indent crimper, sizes 12 / 16 (P038)
Wire strippers 10-22 AWG, flush cutters (P043)
Ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices, rings and spades (P171)

done_when: One labelled bag per switch position in the lists above, each with a resistor (and its diode where named) on two 4 in leads under heat-shrink, each measured within 1 % of its value and the reading written on the bag.

goal: The factory battery and its two cables are out, and the Ionic battery sits in the cargo bin on its backing plate, held down so it cannot move, with both terminals booted and nothing connected.

done_when: The factory battery and both its cables are out and bagged; the fusible-link block is still on the car with its battery-side lead taped and labelled; the Ionic is clamped on its backing plate and does not move when pushed hard in every direction; both terminals are booted; nothing is connected to it.
if_not: The battery moves under a hard push: do not go on - re-make the hold-down or the plate. goal: The master disconnect and the Class-T fuse block are mounted beside the battery, the rear ground stud is made on bare metal, and the three short battery cables are cut, crimped, booted and bolted on - with the fuse out, the switch off and the negative lug still off the battery.

Heat gun (P042)
Torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N·m (P046) - and a larger one if a maker's figure is above 20 N·m (none is in the parts table)

Drill

Paint pen (from P082)
Eye protection
before:
E8 is done: the Ionic is held down, booted, unconnected

Eye protection for grinding and crimping
The Class-T fuse stays OUT all weekend
know:

C12: battery + clamp stud to the disconnect's INPUT stud, 1/0 red, 1.0 ft - a hand estimate, confirm. It is the one cable no fuse protects: keep it to inches [cables C12; D-062]
C01: the disconnect's OUTPUT stud to the Class-T block's input, 2 AWG red, 1.0 ft - a hand estimate, confirm. Its lug sits on the output stud UNDER the MRBF fuse holder that goes on at E10 [cables C01]
C05: battery - clamp stud straight to the rear ground stud, 1/0 black, 3 ft - a hand estimate, confirm. The negative is never switched [cables C05; backbone B5]
Lugs: 1/0 are P098 (3/8 in hole for the disconnect, the ground studs and the clamp studs; 5/16 for the MRBF holder), 2 AWG are P064 (5/16 and 3/8 holes) - the hole at each stud is confirm until the studs are measured [parts P098, P064, P095; checks CK24]

The same stud is the rear star: the table also holds a 10 AWG conductor from it to the chassis (G23, 2 ft, confirm), which the row's note does not mention [grounds G23; cables C14]
Every lug gets heavy-wall adhesive shrink and a boot [work E9; parts P066, P077]

The positions of the switch, the block and the stud come from the M-4 mock-up; none is in the record [work V-088]
done_when: Disconnect and Class-T block mounted; rear ground stud on bare metal, waxed; C12, C01 and C05 made with a lug, heavy-wall shrink and a boot at each end, labelled; C12 and C01 bolted and torqued; C05 bolted at the stud with its battery end off and insulated; switch OFF, Class-T fuse out; meter shows continuity through the switch ON and open with it OFF.
if_not: A lug that turns on its cable or shows strands: cut it off and crimp a new one (the spares are for this). A hole that does not match its stud: stop, note the sizes, and do not drill a lug out. No continuity through the switch when ON: check each nut and the switch itself before going on.
record: Tick the row. Note the three cables' real cut lengths (C12, C01, C05) and the torque you used at each stud in the app.

goal: The starter feed, the cranking return and the PMU feed run from the cargo bin through the tunnel to the engine bay and the dash; the front ground stud, the engine-to-chassis strap and the two MIDI fuse holders are fitted; everything is still dead, fuses out.
where: cargo bin, the tunnel, under the car, engine bay and the dash-node position
tools:
Hydraulic lug crimper, 8 AWG to 1/0, with dies (P037)
Ratchet crimper for insulated and heat-shrink terminals, 22-10 AWG (P171)
Heat gun (P042)

Drill
Jack stands and wheel chocks
Multimeter on ohms (P045)
Label printer (P041)
Paint pen (from P082)
Eye protection
before:
E9 is done: disconnect OFF, Class-T fuse out, the negative lug off the battery
The console and tunnel trim are out (S1) and the tunnel was measured for three heavy cables (C1, M-2)
Car on jack stands, wheels chocked, for the starter and the block
Engine cold
Eye protection for grinding and crimping
know:
The MRBF fuse holder is a Blue Sea 5191 (P051); it bolts on the master disconnect's OUTPUT stud, not on the battery post, with C01's lug under it. Its 250 A fuse (P052) is NOT fitted yet [fuses MRBF; cables C02; parts P051]
C04, the starter feed: 1/0 red from the MRBF holder to the starter's main B+ stud, 18 ft - a hand estimate, confirm [cables C04; devices DV02]
C11, the cranking return: 1/0 black from the rear ground stud to the engine block, 18 ft - a hand estimate, confirm; pulled beside the starter feed. Without it 400 A would cross the whole body shell [cables C11; backbone B7]
C03, the PMU feed: 2 AWG red from the Class-T block to the dash post, 16 ft - a hand estimate, confirm [cables C03]
All three go through the tunnel, loomed, P-clipped every 12 in, with a grommet at every pass-through [routes RT15; work E10]
C03 ends for now on a temporary insulated post, a Blue Sea 2003 PowerPost with a 3/8 in stud (P050), mounted where the dash node will go [parts P050; work E10]
A pull string goes in beside C03 before the console goes back [work E10; parts P081]
Front star stud (G05): on the radiator support, bare metal, 3/8 stud, star washer, torque, wax; plus a 10 AWG black wire, 2 ft estimated, from the stud to a second body bolt [grounds G05; work E10]
C06, the engine block to chassis strap: 2 AWG black, 2 ft estimated, 24 in or less. It is the bond, not the cranking return [cables C06; backbone B6]
F17 (30 A) and F18 (100 A) are MIDI fuses in Blue Sea 7720 holders (P053, M6 mounting) beside the starter B+ stud [fuses F17, F18; parts P053, P054, P055]
C07: alternator B+ to F18 to the starter B+ stud, 6 AWG red, 4 ft estimated, lugs P065 (5/16 hole, confirm) [cables C07; parts P065]
F17 feeds the start relay K9 and stays unwired until K9 is wired at E27 (the row's note says E38, an old row number) [fuses F17; work E27]
Lugs: P098 for 1/0 (5/16 hole at the MRBF holder, 3/8 at the ground studs and the block), P064 for 2 AWG - holes confirm against the studs measured at CK24 [parts P098, P064; checks CK24]
Not in the record: which bolt on the block and on the chassis each ground cable lands on, where exactly the MIDI holders mount, and whether the factory wire already on the alternator's B stud stays - note what you do [work E10; devices DV04]
done_when: C04, C11 and C03 lie loomed and clipped through the tunnel with every end lugged, shrunk, booted and labelled; C04 is on the starter stud and the MRBF holder; C11 and C05 share the rear ground stud, torqued and waxed; C03 is on the Class-T output and the temporary post; the front star stud and its 10 AWG wire, the block strap and both MIDI holders are fitted; the pull string is in; the meter shows the continuities in the steps; both big fuses are still out.

record: Tick the row. Note the real lengths of C03, C04, C11, C06 and C07, the bolts used for the block and chassis ends, and the torques, in the app.

goal: The factory harness takes its supply from the temporary post through its own fusible links and its ground from the front star; the Class-T and MRBF fuses are in; the battery is connected; and the Ionic app shows the pack's voltage, charge and temperature.
where: engine bay, the dash-node position and the cargo bin
tools:
Spanners for the post, the stud nuts and the battery clamps
Torque wrench (P046)
Multimeter on DC volts (P045)
Ratchet crimper for insulated terminals (P171) and heat gun (P042) if a ring is needed
Phone with the Ionic app
Paint pen (from P082)
before:

Disconnect OFF, both big fuses out, the negative lug still off the battery, until the steps say otherwise
Your E8 notes on the factory cables are in front of you
Rings and watch off; extinguisher within reach

The factory harness's main feed is the black 1.25 sq main fusible link (PT317) in block X-07, with a brown 0.3 sq link either side of it (PT316) for the headlight retractors and the headlights [00-CAR PT317, PT316]
The 1985 manual places the fusible links at the front left suspension tower - 1985 manual, confirm on the car [00-CAR SP-063]
The factory feed keeps its fusible links in series on the post: nothing of the factory protection is bypassed [work E11]
The post is the Blue Sea 2003 PowerPost fitted at E10, fed by C03 from the 150 A Class-T [parts P050; cables C03]

The factory harness's main ground moves onto the front star stud made at E10 [work E11; grounds G05]
Class-T fuse: 150 A, Blue Sea 5114, two bought - one fitted, one spare. MRBF fuse: 250 A in the 5191 holder [parts P048, P052; fuses Class-T, MRBF]
The negative cable goes on last [S-002 p.5-5]
The Ionic's output range is 8.0 to 14.6 V; it read 13.0 V, 3.25 V a cell, on 2026-09-08 [00-CAR SP-232; D-330]
The pack's published operating range is -20 to 60 C [00-CAR SP-233]
Never start a firmware update on the pack: that path can brick the battery that runs the car [D-330]
The cluster is unplugged and the interior is out, so the car is not started today: that is E12 [work E12; D-387]
Not in the record: what conductor joins the fusible-link block (in the bay) to the post (at the dash), and which factory wire is the "main ground" - use your E8 notes [work E11; 00-CAR PT290]

goal: The engine starts and runs on the new backbone, the alternator charges the Ionic at or under 14.6 V, both cranking voltage drops are under 0.5 V, and every factory circuit works exactly as before.
where: cargo bin and engine bay, the car stationary
tools:
Multimeter on DC volts (P045), with min/max hold if it has it
A long jumper lead to extend one meter probe from the cargo bin to the engine bay - not in the parts table: any light wire will do
An assistant on the key
Wheel chocks
Extinguisher within reach
before:
E11 is done: fuses in, battery connected, the app reading
Garage door open; belt and fan clear of leads, sleeves and tools
Car in P, wheels chocked: the seats are out and it is not driven
Extinguisher within reach
know:
The factory cluster was unplugged at the strip (S1): re-plug it so the meters read; the tachometer gives you 2,000 rpm [work E12]
Charging voltage at the battery at 2,000 rpm: expect 13.8 to 14.6 V [work E12]
The Ionic's maximum charge voltage is 14.6 +/- 0.1 V. Above about 14.7 V the fix is the alternator's regulator, never the battery [checks CK03; 00-CAR SP-231]
The factory regulated band is 14.2 to 15.2 V, so a healthy factory alternator can be too high for this battery [00-CAR SP-081]
The check asks for the reading with headlights off, then with headlights and blower on, engine warm [checks CK03]
This car has shown no charge before: 11.4 V at idle. The new excitation circuit that should cure it comes at E28 (F15, migration step MG21) [D-198; work E12]
Voltage drop while cranking, battery + post to starter stud, and battery - post to engine block: each under 0.5 V; near 0.5 V means a bad crimp [work E12]
Cranking pulls 300 to 500 A briefly [backbone B2]
By the wire table 18 ft of 1/0 is about 0.0018 ohm, which by itself drops 0.5 V at about 280 A: a hard crank can read a little over 0.5 V on the cable alone - record the figure either way [awg 1/0; cables C04, C11; arithmetic]
Shut the engine down before opening the master disconnect [recovery RC01]
No driving: the interior is out until E35 [D-387]
done_when: The engine starts and idles; the battery reads between 13.8 and 14.6 V at 2,000 rpm; each cranking drop is under 0.5 V; lamps, wipers, horn, blower and the other factory circuits work as they did; the three readings are entered in E42, E43 and E44.
if_not: It does not crank: disconnect ON? MRBF in? C04 tight at both ends? It cranks but does not charge (battery voltage does not rise above the resting figure): stop running it - the alternator or its excitation is the cause, and E28 rebuilds the excitation; do not run long on the battery alone. Above 14.6 V: stop, note the figure, raise it in the app (the regulator). A drop of 0.5 V or more: find the warm or loose lug on that side and re-make it, then repeat.
record: Tick the row; it asks for a value in V - enter the charging voltage, the same figure as E42. Then enter E42 (V), E43 (V) and E44 (V) in their own rows.

goal: The charging voltage at the battery at 2,000 rpm is measured and entered, and it is at or under 14.6 V.
where: cargo bin, at the battery posts
tools: Multimeter on DC volts (P045)
before:

Multimeter on DC volts (P045), min/max hold if it has it
The long jumper lead from E12
An assistant on the key

The starter feed C04 is 18 ft of 1/0, estimated [cables C04]
By the wire table that cable alone drops 0.5 V at about 280 A, and cranking is put at 300 to 500 A: a figure a little over 0.5 V on a hard crank may be the cable - record it either way [awg 1/0; backbone B2; arithmetic]

record: Enter the value in V.

goal: The voltage drop from the battery - post to the engine block while cranking is measured and entered, and it is under 0.5 V.

Multimeter on DC volts (P045), min/max hold if it has it
The long jumper lead from E12
An assistant on the key
before:
Taken at E12 step 10, straight after E43
Car in P, wheels chocked; clear of belt and fan
know:
Probes: battery - post to the engine block, read while the starter cranks [work E44]

tools: Phone with the Ionic app
